title: Majestic Endgame
reviewNotes: All ten source diagrams re-reviewed, including native final c7+ fork. The seven-piece lesson root is explicitly derived by independent legal ...Qxc7 from that complete eight-piece source position; no unseen source move is invented. bxc7+ is the only winning root move; independent Kc8/Kd5/Kxc7/c6 retains the second passer and White g2/Black g3. Earlier eight-piece plan and other Black fork defenses remain outside proof.
transcript: Sometimes the most beautiful tricks are hidden in the simplest positions. In this situation, it seems like white is completely lost. It has four pawns against the queen and one pawn of black. Black is just going to pick up the last pawns and win the game easily, right? Well, not exactly. It is white to move and there is a way for white to bounce back and not only draw the game but win this game. And as you can imagine, the first move is B6 check. The only check that we have available in the position. Black cannot capture this pawn, of course. And importantly, the king cannot step to this square because this will end up being a fork, picking up the queen and winning the game. But black still has a resilient square to go to. The king can go to C8. And it seems like black is out of the woods. But here is where white plays the absolutely brilliant king E4. A completely counterintuitive move, but that strips away the black queen of every single square available to her. Meaning that black is actually in zukswang in this position. There are no moves available that don't lose the queen, which means that black will have to move the king. But we already know how this goes. And we are going to pick up the queen and win this
